items.stem: Find the value of k for which the lines 3x + y + 12 = 0, −2x − y − 8 = 0 and kx + y + 9 = 0 are concurrent.
items.markingKey: The first two lines meet at (−4, 0) (2); this point lies on the third line: −4k + (0) + (9) = 0 (1) ⇒ k = 9/4 (1).

items.stem: Find the distance between the parallel lines 3x + 4y + 10 = 0 and 6x + 8y + 24 = 0.
items.markingKey: Divide the second equation by 2 so that the x and y coefficients match (1); d = |C₁ − C₂|/√(A² + B²) = |−2|/√25 = 2/5 (1).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about forms of the equation of a line is correct?
items.answer: A line parallel to the y-axis at distance a from it is x = ±a.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: "A line parallel to the y-axis at distance a from it is x = ±a." The other three are false.
options: The equation of the y-axis is y = 0.
The two-point form needs the slope to be given.
A line parallel to the y-axis at distance a from it is x = ±a.
The line through (2, 3) parallel to the x-axis is x = 2.

items.stem: Find the points on the x-axis whose perpendicular distance from the line 5x + 12y + 23 = 0 is 4 units.
Find the perpendicular distance of the point (2, 6) from the line −5x + 12y + 8 = 0.
Find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular from (1, 4) to the line 3x + 4y + 6 = 0, and the image of the point in the line.
items.markingKey: The perpendicular through the point has direction (3, 4) (1); write (x, y) = (1, 4) + t(3, 4) and substitute in the line (1); t = −1 gives the foot (−2, 0) (1); the image is at twice the distance: (−5, −4) (1).

items.answer: If m₁m₂ = 1, the lines are perpendicular.

items.stem: Reduce 5x + 12y − 52 = 0 to the normal form x cos ω + y sin ω = p and find p, cos ω and sin ω.
items.markingKey: √(A² + B²) = 13 (1); divide by 13 and keep the constant on the right positive: (5/13)x + (12/13)y = 4 (1); read off p, cos ω and sin ω (1).

items.stem: The vertices of triangle ABC are A(6, 0), B(3, 6) and C(−1, 2). Find the equations of (i) the median through A and (ii) the altitude through A.
items.markingKey: (i) Midpoint of BC is (1, 4) (1); line through A and it (2): 4x + 5y − 24 = 0. (ii) Slope of BC, then the perpendicular slope through A (1): x + y − 6 = 0 (1).

items.stem:
On a district map (1 unit = 1 km), the new highway is the line 5x + 12y − 48 = 0 and the village Sitapur is at (4, 1). A straight link road is to be built from Sitapur to the highway.
(i) What should be the direction of the link road for it to be shortest? (ii) Find the length of the shortest link road. (iii) If the road costs ₹3 lakh per km, find the cost. (iv) Find the slope of the link road.
items.answer: (i) perpendicular to the highway (ii) 16/13 km (iii) ₹3.69 lakh (iv) 12/5
items.markingKey: (i) Shortest distance is along the perpendicular (1). (ii) |Ax₀ + By₀ + C|/√(A² + B²) (1). (iii) length × rate (1). (iv) negative reciprocal of −5/12 (1).

items.stem: Find k if the line through (−2, 1) and (−4, 2) is perpendicular to the line through (−2, 3) and (k, 9).
Find the point of intersection of the lines −x + 3y − 4 = 0 and −x + 4y − 7 = 0.
items.markingKey: Solve the two equations simultaneously (elimination) (1): x = 5, y = 3 (1).

items.stem:
An auto-rickshaw in Pune charges ₹104 for a 4 km ride and ₹184 for a 9 km ride. The fare y (₹) is a linear function of the distance x (km).
(i) Find the slope of the fare line and interpret it. (ii) Write the equation of the line. (iii) What is the fare for 21 km? (iv) What does the y-intercept represent?
items.answer: (i) 16, the charge per km (₹16/km) (ii) y = 16x + 40 (iii) ₹376 (iv) the fixed (minimum) charge ₹40
items.markingKey: (i) (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) (1). (ii) two-point form (1). (iii) substitute x (1). (iv) value at x = 0 (1).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the general equation of a line is correct?
items.answer: In the normal form x cos ω + y sin ω = p, p is the length of the perpendicular from the origin.

items.markingKey: The first two lines meet at (−1, 3) (2); this point lies on the third line: −1k + (6) + (−7) = 0 (1) ⇒ k = −1 (1).
